memory_candidates.content: A reach mechanism for domain-specific plan-authoring guidance (a gotchas/checklist file under context/project/<domain>/) should be a task_type-gated lookup performed INSIDE a shared agent's own file (e.g. planner-agent.md Stage 4), never an agents[] entry added to the domain's context index entry. context-discovery.md's adaptive query ORs the agent/task_type/command dimensions, so a cross-domain shared agent (planner-agent, general-implementation-agent, general-research-agent) named in a domain-specific entry's agents[] leaks that domain's content into every other domain's dispatch of that agent. Domain-exclusive agents tolerate the same OR semantics harmlessly since they never run for a non-domain task.

A bash fail-open reader function parameterized on a repo_root that is legitimately empty in the ordinary absence case must use ${1:-} for that parameter, never a required-argument guard like ${1:?msg} -- the colon-form treats an empty string the same as unset, so under set -euo pipefail a required-argument guard aborts the whole calling script outright on the ordinary fail-open path instead of degrading gracefully. Caught via the phase's own named test suites (not narrow unit fixtures alone), which exercise the reader end-to-end via a real subprocess invocation in an isolated fixture root with no repo marker up to filesystem root.
